texts.preamble: Sh. Mansa Ram vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 14 May, 2016 1 In The Court Of Sh. Rakesh Pandit, Asj-01, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Ca No. 85/15 Sh. Mansa Ram S/o Sh. Ishwar Dass, R/o Rz-C-3-32, Sitapuri, Part-1, New Delhi. ....A Vs. The State (Delhi Administration) .... Date of receiving of Appeal : 22.09.2015 Date of arguments : 11.05.2016 Date of judgment : 14.05.2016 Judgment
texts.facts: 2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Kadimi Sweets Pvt. Ltd. at C-5A Market, Janakpuri, New Delhi-58. On 20.11.2002 at about 2.30 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. V. P. S. Chaudhary visited the said place and purchased 1500 grams of " Laddoo Motichoor" from accused. FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. M. A. Ashraf. The said Laddoo CA No. 85/15 Mansa Ram Vs. State page 1 of 6 Motichoor was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act. The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA. Panchanama was prepared. One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst. During investigation, it was found that the said establishment has appointed Sh. Mansa Ram as its nominee under PFA Act. As per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is adulterated because Total dye content of synthetic colour used exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 100 PPM (428.59 PPM)." Sh. Mansa Ram vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 14 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78476118/ 1 3 As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 28.03.2003 with the court. Accused was summoned. He has exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act to get the sample analyzed by CFL. CFL reported "I am of the opinion that the above sample contravenes Rule 30 of the PFA (Tartrazine 335.0 PPM Sunset Yellow FCF 25.0 PPM Total dye 360.0 PMM). 4 Charges were framed against accused company as well as nominee Mansa Ram u/sec.2(ia) (a) (j) (m) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act. He remained in custody for two days. CA No. 85/15 Mansa Ram Vs. State 6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:- (i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule i.e. independent witnesses were not joined (argued orally though not in grounds of appeal). (ii) There is variation in different reports (PA and CFL) so the sample was not properly homogenized. (iii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, spoon, tray etc., were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official. (iv) Excessive fine beyond the purview of PFA Act and beyond the jurisdiction of trial court. 7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
texts.arguments: This CA No. 85/15 Mansa Ram Vs. State page 3 of 6 line of argument was done before the trial court and was dealt in para 44 to 90 of the judgment. However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food. If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis. So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers". Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean. Similarly, in other judgments, CA No. 85/15 Mansa Ram Vs. State page 4 of 6 like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean. Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not proved to be clean and dry. 13 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement" or any other surface, it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement/surface was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.
